html:
SMTO-PSM-0002 — SMTO couldn't understand the type-in instruction in your message

GUID: d3cfad3a-b78b-4820-bd7d-91eb6a29da97
Slug: user-macro-invalid
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • Your message asks SMTO to type a value into a command, but the instruction is incomplete or points to more than one saved value. SMTO didn't type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you wrote typein followed by a value, put the value in straight double quotes and close them, for example typein "my value". SMTO needs a complete quoted value to know exactly what to type.
  2. Use only one type-in instruction in each message. SMTO can type in just one value per message.
  3. To type a value saved in the Parameter Store, give the parameter's exact name and the field, for example typein password from my-server. When several parameters or fields match, SMTO won't guess which one to type.
  4. Open Parameter Store and check that the parameter exists and has the field you named. The error message lists the fields that parameter actually has, so you can pick the right one.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts your message and the Agent types the value into the command.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste a secret value into your message instead; keep it in the Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • User macro parsing rejected a typein instruction: an unterminated or non-string quoted value, more than one typein, an unavailable Parameter Store, no or several matching records, or no single scalar field to type.

What this means

  • Macro parsing rejects malformed quoted syntax, missing/ambiguous parameter selection, unavailable parameter lookup, incompatible modes or absent/multiple scalar fields for typing. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Macro parsing rejects malformed quoted syntax, missing/ambiguous parameter selection, unavailable parameter lookup, incompatible modes or absent/multiple scalar fields for typing.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the named macro and exact selected parameter field; separate syntax from ambiguous lookup.

How to fix it

  • The message in Technical details names the specific parser failure in agent_runtime/api/macros/user_macros.py. Use the exact syntax typein "value" with one typein per prompt, or reference one Parameter Store key and one scalar field (for example "typein password from" followed by the exact key), and make sure the Parameter Store is available to the request.
  • Correct the exact macro syntax or choose one eligible parameter field through the supported reference flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported macro resolves one intended scalar/action without exposing stored secrets.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
